motivation: Miyasaka first used organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites as photovoltaic absorbers (2009). Park (2012) and Snaith (2012) then showed solid-state perovskite cells, and Snaith showed that these solution-processed films carry charge over long distances as ambipolar semiconductors. That finding overturned the assumption that only highly purified crystals could give efficient photovoltaics. Within a decade, single-junction efficiencies went from about 4% to above 26%, and perovskite-silicon tandems now exceed the Shockley-Queisser limit for silicon alone. The discovery opened a new area of semiconductor physics: defect-tolerant band structures, mixed ionic-electronic conduction, ion migration and polaronic carrier dynamics. These have changed how we model disordered absorbers. Perovskite tandems are now being commercialised, so the work also bears directly on low-cost decarbonisation of electricity supply.
